terms.x: two ways to reach one value
terms.p: Having more than one path to the same piece of memory, which is harmless on its own and dangerous the moment one of those paths can write.

terms.x: a borrow ends at its last use
terms.p: The rule, since the 2018 edition, that a borrow lasts until the last place it is used rather than until the end of the block it was created in.
A shorter borrow taken through an existing mutable reference, which freezes the original for its duration and then hands it back.
Borrowing two different fields of the same value at once, which is allowed because the compiler tracks each field path separately.

terms.x: the reference that outlived its buffer
terms.p: A reference or iterator into a collection left pointing at freed memory because the collection grew and moved its contents elsewhere.
